subjects.label: Dams and water physics
subjects.description: Building dams, levees, sluices and aqueducts and how the simulated water then flows, floods or strands a village downstream; praise for the building sandbox that never mentions water does not belong.

subjects.label: Drought, badwater and water storage
subjects.description: Surviving the dry season and badwater: storing water, irrigating fields, working the gates while the river is stopped and what dies when it runs out; dam engineering for its own sake belongs under dams and water physics.

subjects.label: Starvation and food supply
subjects.description: Keeping the colony fed: beavers starving to death, famines, how much they eat, farming and whether food keeps; a shortage of water rather than food belongs under drought.

subjects.label: Mechanics removed or reworked by updates
subjects.description: Features taken away or changed between versions, such as irrigation, water tanks, the sluice or a difficulty rebalance, and players asking for the old version back; whether the developers are active at all is plain updates.

subjects.label: Slowdown as the colony grows
subjects.description: Frame drops, lag and crashes that only appear once the settlement is large or the session long, growing with beaver count and buildings; a game that runs badly from the first minute is plain performance.

subjects.label: The district system
subjects.description: Districts as a mechanic: being forced to split the settlement, resources stranded on the wrong side of a border, goods handed over at district edges and the prompt to build a road or a new district; expansion complaints that never mention districts do not belong.

subjects.label: Folktails and Iron Teeth
subjects.description: The two playable beaver factions, how they differ, which is stronger and the wish for more of them; the beaver premise in general belongs elsewhere.

subjects.label: The beaver premise
subjects.description: Beavers as the thing the game is about: wanting to be one, their habits and cuteness, and the bobr jokes and beaver puns the premise invites; a verdict that never mentions beavers does not belong.
